description: Every alert rule a vault position or watch can be, said exactly: its wording with the proposed threshold (e.g. "Reported liquidity falls below my position", "Share price falls 5% from its peak over our record", "An exact match appears among addresses we screen"), the metric and its denominator, the source, how old an input may be before the rule stops counting it, how long a price or rate crossing must hold, the cooling period, whether it is an economic alert or a data-quality notice, and what it does when data is missing. Free. Rules fire on a crossing, once per crossing with an event id, never on an input past its age limit; delivery is at least once, not exactly once. Setting a rule needs an account (PUT /v1/watches) and, except for the free data-quality notices (stale, freshness), a plan. Includes "My position value falls X% from its peak", adjusted for your own deposits and withdrawals by a time-weighted index.

kind.description: One rule kind, e.g. liquidity, simulation, keys. Leave out for all.

name: alert_rules

data.description: Each rule with kind, rule, condition, unit, proposedThreshold, metric, denominator, source, inputMaxAgeHours, confirmMinutes, cooldownHours, economic, basis, defaultTiming, withoutData and free.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

says.description: What the rules promise and what they do not.

states.description: The settings (enabled, disabled, plan required, monitoring unavailable) and evaluations (normal, triggered, unknown, delayed) a rule reports. Missing data is never normal.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.

title: The alert rules, said exactly
